items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I know with the piano that we heard at Mrs. New Iberia, who was I speaking of a far ago? Chewy? No. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. That's over there.

ctx.x: Well, no, that time, we didn't fake nothing at all. We just read. We didn't know. We just had to read music. Oh, everybody read. Everybody read, because we were being taught by this fellow Kerry.

Oh, I see. Let me ask you this. Did you ever have to transpose and change keys because some of the instruments were out of pitch? Oh, yeah, we had. Constantly doing that, huh? Sure, we had. So then you had to do it at full speed and transpose, too? That's right. I've often wondered about that because I know with the piano that we heard at Mrs. New Iberia, who was I speaking of a far ago? Chewy? No. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. That's over there. I just wondered because I knew they must have…

I don't have it no more. I gave it up the very time that I gave up music, I gave it up. You see I got sick in 1924. Well I'll declare. And in 25 the doctor claimed that I would never be able to handle that instrument anymore. Is that right? And I went through it anyhow. I played it up until 25. You see I got sick in 24. But I played it until 25. I got sick in the New Orleans country club. I was playing the afternoon tea, you know, I used to play afternoon tea too. Not only dinner dance but we used to play…
